summary: Rocuronium bromide is a nondepolarizing aminosteroid neuromuscular blocking agent with rapid-to-intermediate onset and intermediate duration, used as an adjunct to general anesthesia to facilitate tracheal intubation (including rapid sequence) and to provide skeletal muscle relaxation during surgery or mechanical ventilation. CRITICAL: it paralyzes but provides NO sedation, analgesia, or amnesia - patients must be ventilated and adequately anesthetized. Effects are reversed by sugammadex or anticholinesterases.
indications: Adjunct to general anesthesia to facilitate routine tracheal intubation
Skeletal muscle relaxation to facilitate mechanical ventilation

dosage.n: Intubating conditions in ~1-2 min; block ~31 min duration
Higher dose gives faster onset (~55-75 sec) and longer duration
Guided by nerve stimulator; do not give until recovery evident
Start after early spontaneous recovery; titrate to response
Onset and duration vary with age; titrate

admin: Intravenous use only; administered by clinicians experienced with neuromuscular blockers
ENSURE the patient is sedated/anesthetized and ventilation is controlled - drug gives no sedation or pain relief
Use a peripheral nerve stimulator to assess depth of block and recovery
May be given by bolus or continuous infusion; do not mix in the same line with alkaline solutions (e.g., barbiturates) - precipitation
Have reversal agent (sugammadex or neostigmine + anticholinergic) and airway equipment available
moa: A nondepolarizing aminosteroid neuromuscular blocker that competitively antagonizes acetylcholine at nicotinic cholinergic receptors of the motor end-plate, preventing depolarization and causing skeletal muscle paralysis. The block is antagonized by acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (neostigmine, edrophonium) and rapidly reversed by the selective binding agent sugammadex.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity (e.g., anaphylaxis) to rocuronium or other neuromuscular blocking agents
relative: Conditions altering response: neuromuscular disease (myasthenia gravis - extreme sensitivity), severe hepatic or renal impairment (prolonged block)
Use without capacity to support ventilation

preg: Use only if clearly needed. It has been used to facilitate intubation for cesarean delivery by experienced anesthetists; like other NMBs it does not cross the placenta in significant amounts at usual doses. Magnesium given for toxemia can potentiate the block.
lact: Limited data on excretion in milk. Given as a single peri-operative dose with short systemic persistence, brief interruption of breastfeeding is generally considered acceptable.
renal: Renal impairment reduces clearance and may prolong the duration of block; no fixed dose reduction but titrate carefully to neuromuscular monitoring and anticipate slower recovery.
hepatic: Rocuronium is eliminated largely by the liver/bile; hepatic impairment increases volume of distribution and prolongs duration of action - reduce/space doses and monitor with nerve stimulator.

moderate: Aminoglycoside, polymyxin, lincosamide and tetracycline antibiotics (potentiate block)
Local anesthetics, quinidine, calcium channel blockers (enhance block)
minor: Corticosteroids and chronic anticonvulsants (may shorten duration/cause resistance with chronic use)
interactions.alcohol: Not relevant in the controlled anesthesia setting
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic lab interference; monitor neuromuscular function clinically/with stimulator

serious: Anaphylaxis / anaphylactoid reactions (rocuronium is a leading cause of perioperative anaphylaxis)
Prolonged or residual paralysis with inadequate ventilation

monitoring: Train-of-four / peripheral nerve stimulation throughout and before reversal
Adequacy of recovery (sustained head lift, grip, TOF ratio) before extubation
counsel: This is given by the anesthesia team during your procedure to relax your muscles
It does not put you to sleep or relieve pain - separate anesthetic/sedative medicines are always given with it
A breathing machine supports you while the drug is working
Tell your anesthetist about any previous reaction to muscle relaxants or anesthetic drugs
pk: Rapid - intubating conditions in ~1-2 min (0.6 mg/kg); ~55-75 sec at 1.2 mg/kg
Maximum block within ~1-3 minutes depending on dose
Elimination half-life ~1.4-2.4 hours (prolonged in hepatic/renal impairment)
Intermediate - clinical block ~30-40 min after 0.6 mg/kg; longer at higher doses
Refrigerate 2-8 C; once removed may be kept at room temperature up to ~60 days; do not freeze; do not return to refrigerator
pearls: PARALYTIC ONLY - provides no sedation, analgesia, or amnesia: always ensure adequate anesthesia and controlled ventilation
Sugammadex rapidly and fully reverses rocuronium (including profound/deep block), making 1.2 mg/kg RSI safer
0.6 mg/kg is the standard intubating dose; 1.2 mg/kg gives onset approaching succinylcholine for rapid sequence intubation
A leading cause of perioperative anaphylaxis - have resuscitation ready
Effect potentiated by aminoglycosides, volatile anesthetics and magnesium
missed: Not applicable - administered as single doses or infusion by the anesthesia team and titrated to neuromuscular monitoring rather than on a fixed schedule.
overdose: Overdose results in prolonged neuromuscular block and apnea. Primary management is maintaining a patent airway, controlled ventilation, oxygenation, and adequate sedation until spontaneous recovery. Sugammadex provides rapid reversal; alternatively, once recovery begins, an anticholinesterase (neostigmine) with an anticholinergic (atropine/glycopyrrolate) can be used. Monitor with a nerve stimulator until full recovery.
